children: , the consumer-technology and digital-services giant, faced a fresh wearables benchmark Monday as Oura pursued a $15.62 billion valuation in its planned IPO. Apple shares were nearly flat, edging approximately 0.1% higher to $336.46.

Oura plans to sell 50 million shares at $40 to $44 apiece, potentially raising as much as $2.2 billion. The smart-ring maker is growing fast: nine-month revenue climbed 74% to $1.21 billion as consumers increasingly used its devices to monitor sleep, heart rate and physical activity. For Apple, that growth matters less because of Oura's absolute size and more because it shows how quickly specialized health hardware can build a loyal user base outside the Apple Watch.

The valuation picture keeps that competitive threat in perspective. Oura's targeted $15.62 billion valuation is only a fraction of Apple's roughly $4.9 trillion market capitalization, while the chart places Apple at $336.455, about 17.4% above its GF Value of $286.58. That premium suggests investors are already paying up for Apple's scale, ecosystem and recurring-services economics. The bigger question is whether emerging screenless devices can gradually pull health engagement, subscriptions and valuable biometric data away from Apple's watch ecosystem.

title: Apple Edged Higher as Oura Prices a $15.6 Billion Challenge
